questions.q: The goalkeeper plays to the open right teammate. What should that teammate do next?
options: Open up and face the field
Pass straight back to the goalkeeper
Dribble toward our own goal line
questions.explain: Yes. Opening toward the field lets the receiver see forward passes and move the ball up.
choiceExplanations: Yes. Opening toward the field lets the receiver see forward passes and move the ball up.
The route was open for a reason; passing straight back wastes the space he was given.
Going backward toward our goal invites pressure in the most dangerous area.

questions.q: Put the goal kick in order, from first to last.
options: Opponent closes one of the routes
Keeper passes into the open route
Receiver takes it and turns upfield
questions.explain: Yes. Two angles give choices, the opponent can only close one, so the keeper uses the other.
choiceExplanations: Yes. Two angles give choices, the opponent can only close one, so the keeper uses the other.
The opponent can only close a route once teammates are offering two of them.
The keeper passes after seeing which route the opponent has closed.
The receiver turns upfield last, once the pass has arrived.

questions.q: Now the opponent steps into the middle. Which goal-kick pass has the clear route?
questions.explain: Yes. The opponent has moved inside, so the ground route to the right teammate is open.
choiceExplanations: The opponent stands right in that lane, so the pass could be intercepted near our goal.
Yes. The opponent has moved inside, so the ground route to the right teammate is open.
The long kick travels over the opponent into a fifty-fifty contest, while the right route keeps the ball.
